title: PaperRetrieval
description: How one paper's text arrived, and what was tried. Written beside the text it describes, so a later step reading a quote can tell what it is looking at: text recovered from a PDF carries no reference markup and no guaranteed reading order, and a claim resting on it is not the same kind of claim as one resting on tagged article XML. A paper supplied by hand is a route on this record like any other, not a failure.

doi.description: The paper this record is about.

route.description: Where the bytes came from. 'europepmc' = Europe PMC's fullTextXML for the paper's PMC record. 'preprint_server' = the JATS the preprint server hosts. 'unpaywall' = an open-access location an open-access resolver named. 'manual' = supplied by a user and taken in by 'adopt'. 'none' = no route produced anything; the paper has to be asked for.

kind.description: What the stored bytes are, as distinct from where they came from. 'jats' = tagged article XML, which carries reference markup and document order. 'pdf' = a PDF, whose text has to be recovered before it can be read.

path.description: The stored source, relative to the directory holding this record.

text_file.description: Text recovered from a PDF, relative to the directory holding this record. Absent for a JATS source, which is read directly.

sha256.description: Digest of the stored source, so a later run can tell whether the bytes changed rather than re-fetching to find out.

url.description: Where the bytes were fetched from. Absent for a manually supplied file, which has no URL.

title.description: The paper's title, where a route happened to return it. Not looked up on its own account — it is here so that asking a user for a paper can name it.

attempted_at.description: When the waterfall last ran. Together with the attempts below this is the negative cache: a paper that no route could produce is not re-requested on every later pass unless a retry is asked for.

attempts.description: Every rung the waterfall reached, in the order it reached them, including rungs that could not run at all. A rung missing from this list was never tried, which is a different thing from a rung that tried and found nothing.

oa_candidates.description: The open-access locations a resolver named, kept whether or not one was used. Whether a location is the paper or a preprint of it is a judgement, and it cannot be made after the fact from a URL alone.

text_quality.description: What recovering text from the PDF produced. Present whenever text_file is, because a PDF that extracts to almost nothing is a scan, and that is indistinguishable from a paper with little to say unless the size is on the record.

gap.description: What could not be retrieved and what would fix it. Present when route is 'none'.

Attempt.description: One rung of the waterfall and what it did.

route.description: The rung. 'local' is the cache check that runs first and is not a route: where it succeeds the existing record is kept as it stands, so that a paper supplied last week still reads as supplied.

outcome.description: 'ok' = produced the bytes on this record. 'unavailable' = the rung ran and this paper is not reachable by it. 'failed' = the rung ran and broke, so it is worth retrying. 'skipped' = the rung could not run at all, e.g. a missing dependency or no contact address for a resolver that requires one — nothing was learnt about the paper.

note.description: What happened, in enough detail to act on. Free text.

OaLocation.description: One open-access location as the resolver described it. The resolver's own vocabulary is kept verbatim rather than mapped onto ours, so that a value it adds later does not read as invalid.

url_for_pdf.description: A direct link to the PDF, where the resolver has one. Frequently absent even for a location that is genuinely open, in which case only a landing page is on offer.

host_type.description: Whose host it is, as the resolver says — typically the publisher or a repository.

version.description: Which version of the paper, as the resolver says. A submitted version is the manuscript before review, so a location offering only that is a preprint of the paper rather than the paper.

used.description: Whether the bytes on this record came from here.

TextQuality.description: Size and shape of the recovered text, for judging whether it is worth reading.

mean_chars_per_segment.description: A page of scanned images extracts to a handful of very short segments, which this separates from prose.

sample.description: The opening segments as written, so a reader can see whether they are sentences.

Gap.description: A paper no route could produce, said in terms a user can act on.

what.description: The paper, named as well as it is known.

action.description: What would fix it: the file to find, where it can be found, and where to put it.
